observation.title: Observations
observation.intro: Numbers that are not performance: recovery, environment, sensors, body, screening. They are recorded and shown over time — but never rated and never counted into the performance profile.
observation.why: No sound norm exists for any of these values. Putting a “weak” to “elite” scale on them would be invented — and here it could have health consequences.
observation.noMedical: BASELINE does not interpret these values. What a laboratory value means is a doctor’s call, not a sports app’s.
observation.deviceHint: Two devices give different numbers for the same thing. Without this, a course across devices is not one.

sources.self: Can be recorded yourself, without a device.
sources.device: Needs a commercially available measuring device.
sources.lab: Needs specialist equipment or a laboratory.
sources.medical: Needs a blood sample and medical interpretation. The app stores only the number you were given.

meaning.ck_u_l: An enzyme whose blood level rises after unaccustomed load. Variation between people is very large — it is comparable only with yourself.
meaning.doms: Your own rating of muscle soreness on a scale of 1 to 10. Explicitly subjective.
meaning.hrv_rmssd_ms: The variation between consecutive heartbeats. Timing, body position and device shift the value considerably.
meaning.wbgt_c: A measure of heat stress from temperature, humidity and radiation. It describes the environment, not you.
meaning.mip_cm_h2o: Maximum negative pressure when inhaling against a resistance. Needs a device and a practised technique.
meaning.smo2_percent: Oxygen saturation in the muscle under the sensor. A slightly different placement gives a different value.
meaning.fat_mass_percent: The fat share of body mass. DEXA, BIA and skinfolds give markedly different numbers.
meaning.lean_mass_kg: Fat-free mass in kilograms, by the same method as the fat percentage.
meaning.y_balance_composite: A single-leg reach test as a share of leg length. A movement-control screening, not a performance measure.
meaning.fms_total: Seven movement tasks scored 0 to 3 each. A movement-quality screening, not an injury prediction.

procedure.title: How to perform it
procedure.intro: Two measurements are only comparable if the procedure stays the same. Nothing here is a medical recommendation.
procedure.standardise: What has to stay the same
procedure.genericHint: No dedicated procedure is stored for this test yet. What follows comes from the test mode and is more general than a validated protocol.

compare.title: Athlete comparison
compare.intro: Only the same test is compared. Next to every figure is how many of the selected athletes have measured it at all.
compare.noCommon: The selected athletes share no test. A comparison needs at least one test measured by two of them.
compare.axesHint: Share of personal best, not of a norm. Two athletes at 100 are both at their own peak — not equally strong.

gaps.surface: The measurements were taken on different surfaces.
gaps.time_of_day: The measurements were taken at different times of day.
gaps.age_spread: There are {{days}} days between the oldest and the most recent measurement.

group.title: Group report
group.intro: The group as a distribution, not a ranking. Who stands where is what the comparison says.
group.noData: No measurement for this axis exists in the group.
group.medianHint: Median rather than mean: a single outlier shifts the mean by more than a training block shifts the group.

testDay.title: Test day
testDay.intro: One session, several athletes, several stations. The app splits the groups and says who is where, when.
testDay.name: Label
testDay.deleteHint: Only the plan is deleted. The measurements stay with the athletes.
testDay.planHint: Each group moves on one station per round, so no station is ever double-booked.
testDay.sheetsHint: One sheet per station, with the group names and a column to write in. For the clipboard when no device is free.
testDay.incomplete: Not everything is recorded yet. You can still complete the day — the report will then say what is missing.
testDay.needCoach: Test days exist in coach mode. In solo mode there is only one participant.
testDay.notFound: This test day does not exist.
testDay.conditionsHint: Once for everyone. Surface, temperature and equipment are the same for all on a test day — and they are exactly what decides whether two measurements are comparable.
testDay.conditionsApplied: Written to every measurement of this day.
testDay.conditionsMissing: Nothing entered yet. Without it the app cannot later say whether two measurements are comparable.

consent.title: Consent
consent.hint: Whoever keeps other people’s measurements processes personal data. For minors, the consent of a legal guardian is required. The app only records THAT and WHEN consent was given — the evidence stays with you.

state.outgrown: Given as a minor, now of age — own consent required

consent.byHint: The athlete themselves or the consenting person. Nothing beyond the name is stored.
consent.needsGuardian: A minor by date of birth — a guardian’s consent is required.
consent.noBirthDate: Without a date of birth the app assumes the need for protection and requires a guardian’s consent.
consent.blocked: Without consent this app records no measurements for {{name}}.
consent.todoNone: Consent is on file for every athlete.
consent.formHint: A sheet to sign. It stays with you — the app does not store it.
consent.noAdvice: What is required in an individual case is a lawyer’s call. This app gives no legal advice.
consent.formBody: I consent to the person named below taking part in sports-motor performance tests and to the resulting measurements being stored and analysed for the purpose of training evaluation. Consent may be withdrawn at any time for the future without giving reasons. This is not a medical examination.
consent.warn: No consent is on file for {{name}} yet. Measuring works, but the record is missing — for minors the app blocks recording.

onePager.title: One-pager
onePager.intro: One page to pass on — to parents, to a board, to the next coach. The full report remains alongside it.
onePager.noChange: First measurement — a change exists from the second one.
onePager.noData: No measurements exist for this athlete yet.
onePager.disclaimer: BASELINE is not medical diagnostics. This report makes no diagnosis, gives no therapeutic recommendation and assesses no clinical condition. Reference values are a basis for comparison, not a physiological limit; where no published reference exists, the row says so.

meaning.title: What does this mean?
meaning.hint: Four sentences, all computed from your own data. None of them is a medical statement.
meaning.percentile: Of 100 people from the group “{{group}}”, roughly {{below}} would be below your value and {{above}} above it.
meaning.band: The source assigns this value to the band “{{band}}”, relative to {{group}}. It yields no percentile.
meaning.noReference: There is no published comparison group for this test. The value says something about you compared with yourself — and the app claims nothing more here.
meaning.changeFirst: This is your first measurement in this test. A change needs a second one; from the fourth, the app also knows your measurement spread.
meaning.changeUnknown: {{points}} measurements so far. For a sound statement about change the app needs at least four — below that, real progress cannot be separated from measurement spread.
meaning.changeNoise: {{percent}} % difference from the last measurement {{days}} days ago. Your measurement spread is {{detectable}} % — the difference cannot be separated from it and does not count as a change.
meaning.changeBetter: {{percent}} % better than {{days}} days ago. That exceeds your measurement spread of {{detectable}} % and is therefore a real change.
meaning.changeWorse: {{percent}} % weaker than {{days}} days ago. That exceeds your measurement spread of {{detectable}} % and is therefore a real change — not a measurement error.
meaning.limit: So the next measurement stays comparable: {{text}}
meaning.limitGeneric: No dedicated procedure is stored for this test yet. In general: {{text}}
meaning.next: Sensible to measure next: {{test}}. What is trained as a result is a coach’s decision — not this app’s.

group.title: In your group
group.hint: Not a scientific reference value, but the comparison with the athletes who did the same station. It works where no published norm exists.
group.alone: Nobody else in the roster has measured this test yet. From two measurements, a comparison appears here.

metricMeaning.avg_velocity_m_s: Mean velocity over the distance. In short sprints it also contains the acceleration phase.
metricMeaning.fatigue_index_percent: The drop in performance across the effort, in percent. It describes the course within this one test, not fatigability in general.
metricMeaning.ftp_watt: The power sustainable over a longer period, estimated from a 20-minute segment. It depends on the power meter used.
metricMeaning.grip_asymmetry_percent: The difference between both hands, in percent. A side difference is an observation, not a diagnosis.
metricMeaning.grip_relative: Grip strength per kilogram of body weight. Comparable only with the same device and the same arm position.
metricMeaning.hr_drift_percent: How much heart rate rises at constant pace. Heat, hydration and daily form shift the value independently of endurance.
metricMeaning.one_rm_kg: The load that can be moved once. Estimated from several repetitions, it is a computed value, not a lifted weight.
metricMeaning.relative_strength_bw: Load relative to body weight. It also rises when only body weight falls — which is why it stands beside the absolute load, not in its place.
metricMeaning.sinclair_points: A weightlifting factor that makes performances at different body weights comparable. It says nothing about technique or competition ability.
metricMeaning.sjft_index: The Special Judo Fitness Test index: both heart rates divided by the number of throws. Lower is better.
metricMeaning.swft_index: The Special Wrestling Fitness Test index, built the same way as the SJFT. Lower is better.
metricMeaning.vo2max_ml_kg_min: Estimated oxygen uptake per kilogram of body weight per minute. From a field test it is estimated by formula, not measured — a laboratory value would differ.
metricMeaning.watts_per_kg: Power per kilogram of body weight. Wherever your own weight is moved, it says more than raw watts.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.intro: What BASELINE will cost, and what is included.
pricing.notYet: Nothing can be bought yet: there is no payment processing and no contract. This page states what is planned — it is not an order.
pricing.reportsIntro: A report is the print-ready analysis of one test round. Bundles do not expire, there is no subscription and nothing to cancel.
pricing.reportsWhy: Performance diagnostics is periodic: two to four test rounds a year is the usual rhythm. So you pay per report, not per month.
pricing.coachIntro: A seat in your list includes that athlete's reports. Anyone you coach buys nothing on top.
pricing.yourTier: For your {{count}} athletes {{tier}} is enough — {{amount}} € per month.
pricing.yourTierNone: For your {{count}} athletes the tiers are not enough. Talk to us rather than extrapolating a price.
pricing.institutionIntro: At this size the price is agreed, not listed. Which track applies depends not on size but on whether money is made with the diagnostics.
pricing.institutionNoJudgement: The app classifies nobody. It names the criteria — verification happens in conversation, against documents.
pricing.enquiryIntro: The app sends nothing. It assembles the text you send yourself — so you see beforehand what you disclose.
pricing.enquiryNoAthleteData: The enquiry contains no details about individual athletes — only counts and the type of use.
pricing.promiseExport: The export of your data is complete and free — even without a purchased report. Your measurements are yours.
pricing.promiseOffline: Measuring and analysing is free and runs on your own device, even offline. You pay for the report, for sync and for coaching several athletes — not for access to your own values.
pricing.promiseNoExpiry: A purchased report does not expire. No subscription, no notice period, no credit that runs out.
pricing.promiseNoAds: No advertising, no reselling of data, no analysis of your values for other purposes.

imprint.title: Imprint
imprint.intro: Who is responsible for this service.
imprint.name: Name
imprint.incomplete: This imprint is incomplete: {{fields}} still missing. These details must be filled in before public operation — without them the service is not compliant.
imprint.note: Entries without a value are absent, not hidden. They live in src/data/operator.ts.

group.title: Group test
group.intro: One station, every athlete in turn. Made for the test day in the hall: enter a value, move on.
group.stationHint: Test and day apply to every athlete in this round.
group.noAthletes: No athletes exist yet. You can add them in the coach area.
group.rowHint: Empty fields are skipped — whoever was absent gets no value.
group.resultHint: Median and spread, not the mean.
group.caveat: The median rather than the mean, because an aborted attempt or a mistyped value pulls a mean noticeably and a median not. The middle half is the range holding half the group.
group.soloTitle: The group test belongs to coach mode
group.soloBody: In coach mode you manage several athletes and can test them at one station in turn.

coachDash.title: Coach area
coachDash.intro: One row per athlete, sorted by who needs attention. The list should set the work, not the alphabet.
coachDash.name: Name
coachDash.method: The trend is a majority decision across the tests for which one can be computed at all — deliberately not a mean of slopes, because percent per 30 days cannot be meaningfully averaged across different tests. “Needs attention” is not a judgement of the person but a pointer to one of the stated reasons.
coachDash.emptyBody: Add the first person under “Athletes you coach” in your profile.
coachDash.soloBody: This area shows several coached athletes side by side. In solo mode it would be a table with exactly one row — the dashboard says that better.

coach.title: Athletes you coach
coach.hint: Manage several people on one device.

roleHint.solo: One record for you alone. No switcher, no one else's data.
roleHint.coach: Several athletes on this device, switchable from the header. Each has their own record, history and reports.

coach.deleteHint_one: “{{name}}” will be permanently deleted along with {{count}} measurement. This cannot be undone. To hide someone without losing data, use the archive.
coach.deleteHint_other: “{{name}}” will be permanently deleted along with {{count}} measurements. This cannot be undone. To hide someone without losing data, use the archive.
coach.privacyNote: BASELINE stores only what you enter about a coached athlete. No account, email address or invitation is needed. Everything stays on this device.
coach.handoverHint: An athlete moves club or coach: their history belongs to them, not to this device. The file contains only this one athlete — without your branding and without the others.
coach.handoverAdded: Taking on is additive — existing athletes stay untouched.

handoverError.invalid_json: The file is not valid JSON.
handoverError.unknown_format: This is not a BASELINE handover file.
handoverError.newer_version: The file comes from a newer version of the app. Update first.

profile.title: Profile
profile.personHint: Sex and age are required for the reference values
profile.sexHint: There are no sound reference tables for "other" — the percentile view stays empty, everything else works.
profile.bodyWeightHint: Kept as a time series: relative strength needs the weight at test time
profile.recovered: This data came back from the device's second copy, saved on {{date}}. The browser had cleared the main storage.

backupDue.never_exported: You have {{count}} measurements and have never exported. The data lives on this device only — an export makes it yours without it.
backupDue.many_new_results: {{count}} measurements have been added since the last export. A new export takes one click.
backupDue.long_ago: The last export was {{days}} days ago, and {{count}} measurements have been added since.

profile.privacy: Your measurements live in this browser. They are transmitted only if you turn on sync. Clearing browser data removes the local record — the export or sync protects against that.
profile.importFailed: The file could not be read.

importError.invalid_json: The file is not valid JSON. Please choose the unmodified export file.
importError.unknown_format: This file is not a BASELINE export. Your existing data was left untouched.
importError.newer_version: The file comes from a newer version of BASELINE. Update the app to read it — until then your data stays unchanged.
importError.storage_full: There is not enough device storage. Your existing data is unchanged.
importError.unknown: The import failed. Your existing data is unchanged.

profile.contextHint: All optional. What you put here makes reports and comparisons more precise — guessing would be worse than leaving it blank.
profile.levelWhy: Frames the reference comparison. Without it, the comparison is against trained adults.

levelHint.recreational: Regularly active, without a systematic training plan.
levelHint.trained: Systematic training for at least a year.
levelHint.advanced: Several years of structured training with clear progression.
levelHint.competitive: Competing at regional or national level.

profile.sportPlaceholder: only if none of the above fits
profile.trainingAgeHint: Years of systematic training — not your age.
profile.goalPlaceholder: e.g. build endurance, maintain max strength
profile.constraintsPlaceholder: e.g. left shoulder sensitive under load
profile.constraintsHint: Free text for you or your coach. BASELINE does not assess medical conditions and derives nothing from this — the field exists so the context is known when reading the values.
profile.compositionEmpty: Enter a body weight and the composition appears here.
profile.bmiCaveat: Fat mass and fat-free mass are computed from weight and body-fat percentage, not stored separately. BMI does not distinguish muscle from fat and says little about trained people.
profile.disciplineHint: Determines the suggested test battery. Optional — without a selection the general battery stays.
profile.provisionalHint: These numbers rest on a definition made by this app, not on a published formula. They are listed here so nobody mistakes them for documented ones.
profile.provisionalWeights: Also provisional: the requirement weights of the disciplines. They are derived from each discipline’s load structure — competition duration, rest pattern, dominant mode of work — and not taken from a source.
profile.disciplineTestsHint_one: Plus {{count}} further test to choose from, listed in the test catalogue.
profile.disciplineTestsHint_other: Plus {{count}} further tests to choose from, listed in the test catalogue.
profile.sportsHint: The main sport drives overview and recommendations; further sports get their own tests, references and profiles.
profile.goalHint: Weights the next test suggestion — nothing more.
profile.redoOnboardingHint: Takes you through the setup once more. Your measurements are kept — only the details you enter anew change.
profile.legalBody: Imprint, privacy policy and terms of use.
profile.weightClassHint: Where classes exist: combat sports, strength sports.
profile.maturityHint: In adolescents, maturity shifts the result more than chronological age. The app does not estimate it — enter it if you know it.

assessments.title: Assessments
assessments.intro: A test session with a defined scope. Only that makes two points in time genuinely comparable.
assessments.newIntro: Pick a template or compose the tests yourself. On the right you see which axes the session covers — a gap cannot be filled in later without distorting the comparison.
assessments.emptyBody: An assessment bundles several tests into one session and records what scope was measured.
assessments.batteryHint: Compositions for a profile. Ordered by sensitivity to fatigue.
assessments.missingAxes_one: One axis stays unmeasured. The profile will be incomplete.
assessments.missingAxes_other: {{count}} axes stay unmeasured. The profile will be incomplete.
assessments.planHint: Start each test individually. Partial progress is kept.
assessments.finishEarly_one: One planned test is still missing. Completing early is possible; the gap is stated in the report.
assessments.finishEarly_other: {{count}} planned tests are still missing. Completing early is possible; the gaps are stated in the report.
assessments.finishedHint: The session is complete. It can be reopened to add values.
assessments.deleteHint: The session is deleted. The measured results are kept and stay in your history — they only lose their link to the session.
assessments.resultsHint: Percentile against the stored reference, where one exists for sex and age.
assessments.noResults: Nothing has been measured for this session yet.
assessments.summaryGaps: Not measured: {{axes}}. These axes are missing from this session's profile.
assessments.disclaimer: BASELINE is not medical diagnostics. The values describe athletic performance and are neither a diagnosis nor a treatment recommendation. The stored reference values are provisional placeholders and have not yet been reconciled against a published normative sample.
assessments.nextFixed: Set by you. This overrides the app's suggestion everywhere the next session is shown.
assessments.nextSuggested: The app's suggestion based on the usual interval. As soon as you pick a date, your choice applies.
assessments.moreForSportHint: Useful, but not required for a complete profile.
assessments.otherTestsHint: The rest of the catalogue, ordered by capacity.
assessments.generalBatteriesHint: Prepared batteries across all axes — independent of sport. Choosing one here replaces the current test selection.
assessments.noSportHint: Without a sport there is no discipline-specific suggestion. The general assessment below works regardless.
assessments.scopeHint: Every additional test widens the basis: more covered axes mean a more dependable classification and a more complete history. It does not change the precision of the individual measurement.
assessments.alsoIncludedHint: Added from a battery or the rest of the catalogue.

report.printHint: The report becomes a PDF through your browser's print function: Print → destination “Save as PDF”. BASELINE deliberately ships no PDF library — page breaks, typography and selectable text come from your system this way, and it works offline.
report.gaps: Not measured: {{axes}}. These axes are missing from the profile and must be kept in mind when interpreting it.
report.methodConfidence: Confidence is composed in equal parts of axis coverage, recency, data quality and depth. It is unweighted because a weighting could not be justified.
report.methodNorms: Percentiles rest on provisional reference values of this application (baseline_v0_placeholder). They have not yet been reconciled against a published normative sample and should be read as context, not as a normative finding.
report.methodDerived: Derived values: 1RM by Epley, VO2max by Cooper from running distance. Both are estimation formulas; their spread grows with the number of repetitions and with uneven terrain respectively.
report.brandingHint: Name and logo for printed reports.
report.logoType: PNG, JPEG, SVG or WebP only.
report.logoTooLarge: The logo is too large (at most {{max}} kB). A large image bloats the local store.
report.logoUnreadable: The file could not be read.
report.brandingNote: These details stay on this device and appear only in the report. They change no measurement and no analysis.
report.formulaProvisional: Provisional: defined by this app, not a published formula.
report.themeHint: The report follows the chosen appearance: dark stays dark, light stays light. For paper, the light version is worth it — it saves toner and reads better on white.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.intro: What changed over time — and how much that statement can bear. The order is deliberate: a 4 % change across two measurements ten days apart is noise.
analysis.emptyBody: A development needs at least two measurements of the same test. Create an assessment and repeat it after a few weeks.
analysis.confidenceHint: How well is this profile evidenced?
analysis.confidenceFormula: Four parts in equal weight. Deliberately unweighted: a weighting that cannot be justified would be invented precision.

detail.depth: {{deepEnough}} of {{total}} axes measured more than once

analysis.balanceHint: Gap between the strongest and weakest measured axis.
analysis.balanceTooFew: This needs at least two evidenced axes.
analysis.unmeasuredNote: Not counted towards balance because not measured: {{axes}}. Unmeasured is not the same as weak.
analysis.sinceBaselineHint: First against latest measurement per test, with the time span alongside — 4 % in eight weeks and 4 % in two years are not the same statement.
analysis.needTwoPerTest: No test has been measured twice yet.
analysis.changeHint: Direction-adjusted: positive means improved, including for timed tests.
analysis.trendInsufficientHint: A regression line is computed from three measurements onwards. Two points always make a perfect line — that is not a trend.
analysis.compareHint: Completed sessions only. Tests present in just one of the two are marked rather than dropped.

result.societyHint: Only when robust data exist. The app forces no artificial comparison.
result.benchmarkHint: Your result against every matching reference group.
result.noBenchmark: No reference group matches this value.
result.photoHint: One image per result — the timer display, the scale readout. It is downsized and stays on this device; it is not transmitted and not analysed.

photoError.not_an_image: That is not an image file.
photoError.unreadable: The image could not be read.
photoError.too_large: The image is still too large after downsizing. A crop of the display is enough.

result.targetLine: For “{{level}}” this reference requires {{value}} — {{distance}} more than now.
result.targetLineLower: For “{{level}}” this reference requires {{value}} — {{distance}} faster than now.
result.targetHint: The same reference, inverted, with the same assumptions. No statement about whether or how this value is reachable.
result.shareHint: One line to pass on — date, test, value and, where available, the classification.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.intro: Local, no server: the app knows when you last measured. Reminders are off until you switch them on.
reminders.noPush: The reminder appears inside the app when you open it — and, if you allow it, as a system notification at that moment. While BASELINE is closed, nothing arrives: that would need a server knowing who you are and when you last measured, and there deliberately is none. To be reminded without the app, use the calendar file.
reminders.overdueLine: {{test}} has not been tested for {{weeks}} weeks.
reminders.intervalsHint: Interval in days per test. Without a value the default of {{days}} days applies.
reminders.noSuggestion: A suggestion appears from three measurements on.
reminders.calendarHint: One all-day event per due re-test, with an alarm three days ahead. Works in any calendar, offline and without an account — this is the reliable route.
reminders.calendarEmpty: No re-test is due yet. As soon as a test should be repeated, the file will be ready here.
reminders.notifyDenied: System notifications are blocked for this site. Only browser settings can change that.
reminders.notifyUnsupported: This browser has no system notifications.
reminders.notifyLimit: The app can only notify you while it is open — it has no server sending anything in the background. For a reminder that reaches you without the app, use the calendar file.
reminders.notifyBody_other: {{count}} tests are due for a re-test.

modeHint.manual: You perform the test and enter the result.
modeHint.timer: The app runs countdown, effort time and the end signal.
modeHint.series: The app guides you step by step through attempts or stages.
modeHint.external: The value comes from a device or the lab; the app stores and interprets it.

testInfo.scienceHint: Every row is a named group with a source. A reference value is a basis for comparison, not an absolute physiological limit.
testInfo.noScience: There is no published reference for this test. The app invents none — the value stays comparable with yourself.
